notes:
Account snapshot: Opal is a fulfillment and logistics platform powering >1500 3PL partners. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated to replace mixed in-house endpoints — priority is predictable latency under peak batching for reranking + sub-100ms first-token streaming for chat-like support assistants.

Recent activity (short timeline):

- 2026-02-24: SLO alignment workshop with SE (Ravi) and infra (network) — compared client vs server timing (FF: ff_2026-02-24_slo_workshop).

Use-case and SLO requirements (customer language / paraphrase):
- Primary: reranking pipeline for search relevance (low-latency, high-throughput). Need consistent tail latencies during hourly shipping label bursts.
- Secondary: agent assist (streaming) — first-token time critical for UX.
- Target SLOs (Opal initial ask):
  • Non-streaming (batch/rerank): p50 <= 30ms, p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 350ms (measured at Redwood ingress/egress under reserved capacity baseline).
  • Streaming (agent assist - first token): p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 120ms; sustained token throughput (tokens/sec) to be documented per model.
  • Client-view end-to-end targets: p95 <= 300ms non-streaming (includes client network); first-token p95 <= 250ms streaming.

Measurement alignment notes (key asks / risk areas):
- Where to measure: Opal wants both server-side (Redwood edge/router -> model runtime) and client-side (browser/mobile) timestamps for reconciliation. They will require exportable time-series for p50/p95/p99 and raw request logs for a 30-day window for audit.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: define separate SLOs. For streaming, split metrics into first-byte (first token) latency and subsequent token pacing (tokens/sec). Agree on whether p99 applies to first-byte only or both.
- p50/p95/p99 semantics: Opal interprets p95 as the 95th percentile of observed request latencies over 5m sliding windows, aggregated hourly for SLA checks. Redwood's definition must be explicit (windowing, include retries, exclude client timeouts).
- Synthetic vs Production: initial verification with synthetic workload (POC), then shadow/real traffic test for 7 days before final SLA. Need a baseline throughput profile to size reserved GPUs.
- Instrumentation: require consistent request IDs across client and server, epoch-millis timestamps, and token-level timestamps for streaming. Also want lightweight SDK hooks to compute client-side delta and network RTT estimates.

Reserved capacity & throughput planning:
- Current estimate: 12k qps peak for reranking (batched by 8 → effective model tokens/sec). Opal asked for explicit GPU sizing (gpus, slots, per-GPU qps) and autoscaling headroom assumptions.
- Wants an explicit fallback plan when reserved pool exhausted (route to burst pool or smaller quantized model). Impact on latency and cost must be documented for customer sign-off.

SLA negotiation points (legal/commercial):
- Availability SLO target: 99.9% for reserved capacity; penalties TBD if missed.
- Latency SLO measurement source is negotiable: Opal prefers edge-measured p95 for firm commitments but insists on client-side reconciliation window for disputes.
- Data residency & retention: logging exports needed for 90 days; audit logs + KMS key-wrap for models handling PII.

Next steps (actionable):
